summary:
In our project, we have designed an innovative system aimed at creating an additional water source for agricultural irrigation by collecting fog and dew droplets from the atmosphere.
To this end, we will develop a tower system consisting of metal or wooden support rods on the exterior and featuring a wide upper section. Special fog-collecting netting located on the top and sides of the tower will capture fog droplets carried by the wind and convert them into water. Additionally, special dew-collecting surfaces inside the tower will collect droplets formed by the condensation of water vapor in the air under suitable temperature and humidity conditions.
The collected water will be transferred to a water reservoir located at the bottom of the tower via flow channels installed along its length. The water accumulated in the reservoir will be delivered to agricultural fields via a drip irrigation system as needed.
To increase the system’s efficiency, the use of sensors to measure air humidity, temperature, and the water level in the reservoir is planned. Furthermore, the goal is to meet the energy needs of the sensors—and, if necessary, the water pump—with the support of solar panels.
Through our project, we aim to utilize natural water sources such as fog and dew, reduce the reliance on existing water sources used for irrigation, and contribute to sustainable agriculture.
details:
To carry out our project, we will first research fog and dew collection methods, and then build a prototype tower capable of using both methods together.

In the first phase, the tower’s supporting framework will be constructed from metal or wooden rods. A special net capable of capturing fog droplets will be installed on the tower’s wide upper section and side surfaces. Additionally, dew-collection surfaces will be added to the interior of the tower to facilitate the condensation of water vapor from the air under suitable conditions.

In the second phase, the water droplets formed on the fog and dew-collection surfaces will be channeled into a reservoir at the base of the tower via sloped water channels. The accumulated water in the reservoir will undergo the necessary filtration process to make it suitable for agricultural irrigation.

In the third stage, the water collected in the reservoir will be delivered to the plants via drip irrigation pipes. Soil moisture sensors will be used to monitor the plants’ water needs, and irrigation will be scheduled based on those needs.

In the final stage, air temperature, humidity, wind conditions, and the amount of water collected will be measured regularly to evaluate the system’s efficiency. The system’s performance will be evaluated by comparing the results obtained under different weather conditions.

During the project’s experimental phase, the amount of water provided by fog collection and dew collection methods will be determined separately, and then the results obtained by using both methods together will be examined. In this way, the contribution that the developed system can make to agricultural irrigation will be demonstrated with scientific data.
